name: Alternative motion for a resolution
title: REPORT on countering transnational repression – towards an EU strategy to protect Europe’s sovereignty and democratic values
part_text:
The European Parliament is asking the European Union to treat "transnational repression" as a serious problem. This means foreign governments threatening, spying on or harming people who live in Europe but come from their country, often through family members back home. The Parliament wants a shared definition, better data collection, support for victims, and tools to stop countries abusing police, finance and legal systems. It is an opinion and a set of requests; it does not itself change any law.

- **What changes:** Nothing yet. Parliament asks the Commission and member states to act, for example by agreeing a common definition and appointing an EU coordinator.
- **Who it affects:** People in Europe targeted by foreign states, such as exiles, journalists, activists and their families, plus banks, platforms and national authorities.
- **What happens next:** The Commission, Council and member states decide whether to follow the requests; Parliament would need to forward the text to them.
